newsitem.title: USA: CWB says no new wheat shipments going to U.S. PNW.
newsitem.headline: CWB says no new wheat shipments going to U.S. PNW.

text.p: The Canadian Wheat Board said Tuesday that no new shipments of wheat were planned to the U.S. Pacific Northwest (PNW) despite ongoing grain transportation delays in Canada.
CWB spokeswoman Rhea Yates said there had been no further shipments of wheat to the PNW since the one that was disclosed last week, but she left open the possibility of more to come.

"It'll be evaluated on a case-by-case basis," Yates said in a telephone interview. "So if there is a scenario where it would be a benefit to the customer and to the pool accounts, then we would go ahead and do it."
The CWB said last week that it was shipping an "average sized" cargo load of wheat to Portland. The wheat was loaded at Saskatchewan Wheat Pool's Winnipeg terminal.
U.S. PNW grain traders said they were unaware of any more Canadian wheat being railed into Portland for export.
On Tuesday, 43 ships were waiting to load grains and oilseeds on Canada's Pacific Coast, up from 39 last Tuesday. One ship had waited 60 days.
Yates said employees at Canadian West Coast grain terminals had started working two shifts a day, seven days a week, to relieve the backlog.
But she said it was too soon to tell how quickly the added labor input would help clear the situation, because the problem was one of getting grain to the export sites.

"The question is, now that they are going to be available for that full seven days, are we going to be able to utilize them to the full extent?" Yates said. "That's something that in the coming weeks we'll be able to tell whether it's having an effect."
Grain traders on the U.S. Pacific Northwest said they were still trying to figure out who did last week's business.

One Portland exporter speculated that the medium-sized cargo of Canadian wheat was being shipped to the Philippines by Cargill Inc or Continental Grain Co. But traders at those companies declined to comment on the report.
